content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey soufflé is a light, airy dish made from eggs, finely chopped poultry, dairy ingredients and seasonings. During baking the mixture rises, creating a delicate, almost creamy texture. Soufflé is often served as an appetizer or a light main course.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soufflé originates from French cuisine, where the word “soufflé” means “blown up”.
Achieving the airy structure requires carefully beating egg whites to stiff peaks.
Soufflé can be made sweet (with chocolate, fruit) or savory (with meat, cheese, vegetables).
Traditionally it is baked in small ceramic ramekins.
Soufflé loses its shape quickly after leaving the oven, so it is served immediately.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken, turkey and eggs provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When made with lean poultry and modest amounts of cream, soufflé can be relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and poultry contain B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Dairy components add calcium and phosphorus, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Easily digestible protein
items.content: Egg protein is readily absorbed, making soufflé a good option after illness or when higher protein intake is needed.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Soufflé contains a large amount of eggs, which can trigger reactions in people allergic to egg whites.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: If not cooked through, especially with chicken, harmful bacteria may remain.

items.title: Hot serving temperature
items.content: Soufflé is served hot; caution is needed to avoid burns.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or ready‑made sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve soufflé straight from the oven, often with a light sauce, fresh herbs, or a simple salad. It can be eaten with a spoon or cut into portions for a starter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in the oven or a steam bath to retain the airy texture.
